## Who ran it, and how

Lane `check/M0-a-02-close-s3` ran under Opus 5.5 in Claude Code, in a Claude Code cloud container (Linux x64, Node
24.12.0). `tools/machine_profile.py --id` printed `linux:Intel(R) Xeon(R) Processor @ 2.10GHz:4cpu:16gib`, the expected
id. The seat ran on 2026-10-14 from 03:29 to about 07:20. It was resumed once under the CONTINUE RULE after its RELATED
run had finished: the run's log, exit file and done-file were all in the seat's scratch folder, so nothing was re-run
except the fast gates.

This seat is an implementer-side, independent closing checker. It is not the item's author: the author of this round is
`build/M0-a-02-fix-s3` (L-0528, choices C-0361).

The round is the M0 hardening round S3 of M0-a-02 (J237 (2)). It covers the three FIX-NOW rows that
`checks/hardening-inventory.md` (J355) assigns to the item: M0-a-02:12 N-s1-2, M0-a-02:124 N-c2-1 and M0-a-02:125 N-c2-2.

How the seat worked:

* It changed no file of the item and ran no git command.
* Its probes and mutants were planned before it read the author's notes section or self-check lines.
* The pre-round images of the four changed owns were read from main b4759e2's objects by a Python reader (no git). The
  other 22 files of the item's owns are byte-identical to main.
* `tools/test_budget.py` printed 1 every time, so every run used 1 worker. The seat ran one test process of its own at

* Mutants ran in the seat's own mirror, `scratchpad/waves/check-M0-a-02/m`. The mirror is a copy of `plat/` without
  `node_modules`, installed with `--frozen-lockfile`. No link in it points into the tree, and the realpath of
  `@plat/kernel` lies inside the mirror. Its baseline was 117 / 117. Every planted change was restored and checked with
  `cmp`. The mirror's `node_modules` were deleted at the end.
* The item's four changed files are unchanged since 01:07. The seat checked this with `cmp` against copies it took at
  03:39.

* N-c2-1 is **FIXED**. It is a comment-only row, so the text is the deliverable.
* N-c2-2 is **FIXED**. It is a comment row, and its free-list half is also pinned.
* Every gate exits 0. NEAR is 117 / 117, and RELATED@1000 is 463 / 463 files and 5895 / 5895 tests.
* The refusal census is 123 before and 123 after, identical by class, with 0 lawful refusals.
* No executable change was made: the emitted JS with comments removed is identical for all three source files.
* Two new non-blocking notes, N-s3c-1 and N-s3c-2, were added to `checks/M0-a-02-notes.md`.

## (1) The three rows, re-run with this seat's evidence

Each source note was re-read whole (notes lines 12, 124 and 125), and so was the inventory's fix shape for it.

### N-s1-2 (KI): the hole pool's exact fit — PINNED

* **The change.** The growth-preserves-content test in `test/arena/slots.test.ts` ("a capacity-1 arena and a roomy one
  fed the same operations …") now reads every level's `faces[l].holes.length` after each of its 3 000 operations. When a
  pool grew, it asserts both that the pool grew and that its length equals `t.slots.holesTop[l]`. It also asserts
  `poolGrowths ≥ 20`. The note's fix shape asked for an end-of-run check. The per-operation form is stronger, and the
  author is right that a later compaction or clear leaves a pool below full at the end, so the per-operation form
  stands. It matches C-0286 (2) ("a hole pool" grows by exactly what the allocation needs).
* **Mutant A1, K11 re-made by this seat.** In `setFaceHoles`,
  `let cap = tinyTables() ? top + need : t.holes.length * 2;` was replaced by `let cap = t.holes.length * 2;`.
  - On the new test it is **red**: `AssertionError: expected [ 191, 'faces[2].holes', 4 ] to deeply equal [ 191, 'faces[2].holes', 3 ]`.
  - On the pre-round `slots.test.ts` it is **green**, 117 passed (117), so this is a new pin.
* **Mutants A2 – A5.** These are other ways to break exact fit:
  - A2: tiny cap `+1`.
  - A3: `length + need`.
  - A4: a compaction that grows.
  - A5: over-growth.

  All four are red on the new assertion. The first failures were `[121, 'faces[2].holes', 3]` vs `2`, the same vs `2`,
  `[266, 'faces[4].holes', 4]` vs `2`, and `[121, …, 4]` vs `2`. All four are green 117 / 117 on the pre-round test.

A further imprecision that the new wording still carries is noted, as a non-blocker, under N-s3c-1.

### N-c2-2 (comment; C-0286 (2)) — FIXED (comments), with an added pin

The three overstated comments now name the free list, as the source note's fix shape asks:

* `src/arena/debug.ts`: "a growth leaves each exactly full and every allocation of a new slot (one not taken from a
  free list) replaces its table; a slot taken from a free list grows nothing".
* `src/arena/plat.ts`, the `PlatCapacity` header: "makes every allocation of a new slot (one not taken from a free list)
  a growth".
* `src/arena/plat.ts`, the growth section (around line 321): "every allocation of a new slot (one not taken from a free
  list, which grows nothing) replaces it (C-0286 (2))".

C-0361 (2) restates C-0286 (2)'s reading, because the choices file is append-only.

Both files' emitted JS with comments removed is identical before and after. The checker compiled it with TypeScript
`transpileModule` and `removeComments`, through its own `tools/emit.mjs`.

The added assertion in the re-read-premise test ("a growth replaces the table it grows …") was checked with these
mutants:

* **B2** (in tiny mode, a free-list reuse of a vertex replaces `p.vertices` with a copy): red,
  `expected { …(5) } to be { …(5) } // Object.is equality`. Green 117 / 117 on the pre-round test. This is the
  author's FL3, re-made.
* **B3** (tiny mode bypasses the free list): red, `expected 24 to be 23`. Green 117 / 117 on the pre-round test.
* **B1** (a free-list reuse calls `growVertices`; the author's FL2): red through the existing exactness check,
  `'vertices.x': 4195` vs `4096`.

## Refusal census (J264, N-58), re-measured

The census counted every typed refusal message (by class, with digits normalised) raised while the item's arena
folder ran. It was taken twice: on the pre-round images, and on the tree. Both counts are 123, and
the sorted class lists are identical (`diff` empty).

Every class is UNLAWFUL input, deliberately planted by the malformed / size / roles / keys tests, and its verdict is

already carries …", "vertex # is not live". No class is a LAWFUL refusal and none is OUR OWN INTERMEDIATE. The census
did not rise; it is 0 lawful before and after.
